value.rationale: The primary independence test singles out strict PIT nonadditivity as a Gaussian validity condition but leaves concrete boundary behavior open. The constructed score depends on both coordinates, has continuous uniform score distribution and is inside the excluded boundary. Exact finite variance, a complete non-Gaussian n-rate limit and an explicit closed characteristic function answer a nontrivial calibration issue for that precise existing statistic, rather than being a one-line diagnostic or arbitrary numerical slice.
